name: Qoves AI
subcategory: AI portrait analysis and style previews
tagline: Analyze a portrait across six dimensions, then preview a different look.

pricing.notes: The product's public pricing page lists US$7.50 monthly and US$90 yearly; credit usage may affect the practical cost.

verdictSummary: A personal portrait-analysis workflow and reversible style-preview interface are buildable, but matching Qoves AI's analysis quality and hosted image-generation pipeline would require models and services of its own. A local tool can approximate the workflow without claiming equivalent assessments.
coreLoopDIY: Upload one portrait, inspect landmark-based measurements and caveats, and optionally preview a reversible styling change.
requirements: Optional image-generation service credentials for style previews
whatYouLose: Qoves AI's hosted analysis and its particular interpretation of portrait features
The integrated style-preview workflow and managed inference
Any account-based history or product updates
moatNotes: Portrait judgments are subjective; a DIY tool should show measurements and uncertainty rather than present them as objective attractiveness scores.
whyPeopleStillPay: People may prefer a ready-made analysis and style-preview flow over selecting models, managing image processing, and interpreting measurements themselves. Qoves AI's hosted experience is the product; a local recreation would not reproduce its model quality by default.
notes: A DIY version can reproduce the workflow, not the product's model quality or its judgments.
prompt:
Build a private, single-user portrait analysis and style-preview web app.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, and React with TypeScript.
Start from an empty folder and create a runnable project.
Let a user select one local portrait image and preview it before processing.
Keep uploaded images on the user's machine or self-hosted server; document the choice.
Do not add analytics, advertising, accounts, or telemetry.
Use a documented face-landmark library for visible geometric measurements.
Show measurements with plain-language explanations and uncertainty.
Never label measurements as objective attractiveness or medical advice.
Include a clear delete action for every uploaded image and derived result.
Make the analysis usable without a third-party account or API key.
Add an optional style-preview adapter behind an explicit feature setting.
Read any provider credential from an environment variable and provide .env.example.
If no image-generation provider is configured, explain that previews are unavailable.
Keep original images unchanged and make every preview reversible.
Validate file type and size, handle malformed files, and avoid logging image data.
Build accessible labels, keyboard controls, loading states, and useful error messages.
Add a README covering setup, storage, privacy, limitations, and deletion.
Write focused tests for validation and the analysis workflow.
Run the tests and production build before calling the project complete.
